targets.title: Less is more: the lure of ambiguity, or why familiarity breeds contempt
targets.evidence_quote: In a Registered Report with a US Prolific undergraduate student sample ( N = 801) , we directly replicated Studies 1a, 1b and 2 and conceptually replicated Studies 3 and 4 from Norton et al ., 2007.
targets.outcome_quote: We successfully replicated the expectations that knowing a person better would be associated with liking them more, yet failed to replicate the less is more effect proposed by Norton et al . [ 3 ] showing that manipulating knowledge about people impacts liking.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly contrast successful replication of expectations with failure of the less-is-more effect across studies of the same original paper.

reasoning: Completed new-sample direct and conceptual replications of five studies from one original paper. Replication Study 2 also conceptually tests original Study 3. Other literature and materials sources are not targets. Identity and full article/reference boundaries verified.
